summary: A WordPress Stack Overflow question asking how to load a JavaScript file with type="module" (needed to import axios) while still registering scripts in functions.php. The asker first tried a script_loader_tag filter that produced two type attributes, which the accepted-style answer identified as the cause; the asker then posted a working filter that sets type="module" and a later answer notes that WordPress 6.5 added native script module support via wp_register_script_module and wp_enqueue_script_module.
one_line: Stack Overflow question on loading an ES module JavaScript file with type="module" in WordPress via functions.php instead of page template tags.
key_facts: The asker was trying to import axios in a theme JavaScript file and got the error "Uncaught SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module".
The asker's first filter added type="text/javascript" and type="module" to the same script tag, and a commenter noted a script tag can only have one type attribute.
The asker's workaround was adding script tags with type="module" in page.php just above get_footer(), which they disliked because they wanted to register scripts in functions.php.
The question was asked May 8, 2020 and was last modified 29 days before the captured page date.
The question had been viewed 9k times and was tagged functions and wp-register-script.

The asker's final working code registers 'my-script' with get_theme_file_uri('/js/script.js') and dependency ['axios'], then uses a script_loader_tag filter that outputs a script tag with type="module".
The accepted-style answer by Robbiegod was posted November 4, 2021 and suggests that replacing the duplicate type attribute was the fix.
A commenter suggested replacing the regex approach with preg_replace to insert type="module" without removing tag parameters added by other plugins.
Another commenter suggested using str_replace('text/javascript', 'module', $tag) as an alternative.
A later answer states that JavaScript modules have first-class support in WordPress as of version 6.5.
A comment on the 6.5 answer notes that wp_localize_script did not work with script module handles.
The answer author Jon Surrell replied that Script Modules do not support wp_localize_script or wp_add_inline_script.
